Consult Summary:
- Acute diarrheal illness with vomiting and fever consistent with possible infectious gastroenteritis; plan includes hydration, stool testing, and urgent clinic assessment with instructions to seek urgent care if worsening.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Several days of severe diarrhoea with vomiting and fever; user reports very loose stools (initially watery, now very loose), with at least four stools today. Vomiting persists; unable to keep fluids down.
- Onset, duration, progression: Symptoms began 3 days ago and ongoing; no improvement with home measures; vomiting ongoing.
- Associated symptoms: Fever (subjectively "boiling" to touch); nausea/vomiting; abdominal pain around the umbilicus; pain is localized to the central abdomen and worsens with urge to stool; no rash.
- Exposures/trigger: Brother has had similar symptoms; possible school outbreak; patient has been in contact with him.
- Urinary symptoms: Urinating normally; last void about 1 hour ago; urine color not reliably assessed.
- Bowel habit history: Normally one bowel movement each morning; previously healthy bowel pattern; no prior diarrhea or constipation episodes.
- Diet/medications: Attempted oral rehydration salts (ORS) three times daily for past two days; normal diet otherwise; vitamins (vitamin D daily); occasional ibuprofen for cramps.
- Menstrual/gynecologic history: Last period two weeks ago; not on contraception; not sexually active.
- Social history: Graphic designer; lives with mother and brother; non-smoker; occasional alcohol use (a pint occasionally); currently working from home; has missed work.
- Home remedies: ORS prepared; continued use attempted without improvement due to vomiting.

Past Medical History:
- No chronic medical problems documented.
- Menstrual cramps noted; otherwise unremarkable.

Medications:
- Vitamin D (daily) – dose/route not documented.
- Ibuprofen (occasional) – dose/route/frequency not documented.

Allergies:
- Not documented.

Social History:
- Non-smoker; occasional alcohol use.
- Lives with mother and brother; works from home; employed as graphic designer.
- Financial/lifestyle factors not otherwise documented.

Family History:
- Not documented.

Physical Examination:
- Vitals: Not documented.
- Exam findings: Abdominal pain described by patient (periumbilical region); no clinician-reported findings available. No rash or other systemic findings described.

Investigations:
- Stool sample to exclude bacterial infection to guide treatment.
- Hydration assessment planned.
- Sample collection to be done at urgent clinic visit; if clinic collection not possible, samples may be posted.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Acute infectious gastroenteritis with dehydration risk (likely viral; possible bacterial etiologies).
  - Plan:
    - Continue oral rehydration therapy with small, frequent sips to maintain hydration; avoid overfilling stomach.
    - Maintain a light/plain diet if able; avoid fruit, vegetables, and dairy initially; simple foods (e.g., toast, biscuits) as tolerated.
    - Obtain stool sample at urgent clinic visit to assess for bacterial infection and guide treatment.
    - Assess hydration status; monitor urine output (urine within the last hour reported as present).
    - If symptoms persist or worsen, seek urgent evaluation in A&E.
    - Return precautions: call support line to book an urgent clinic appointment; if clinically worse, proceed to urgent care.
    - If stool results suggest bacterial infection, discuss targeted therapy as indicated (not specified in transcript).

- Issue 2: Dehydration risk with ongoing vomiting.
  - Plan:
    - Emphasize continued ORS with small sips; monitor for ability to maintain fluids.
    - In-clinic hydration assessment during urgent visit; advise sooner presentation if dehydration signs develop.

- General plan:
  - Book urgent clinic appointment for hydration check and stool testing.
  - If not improving or if more unwell, come to A&E.
  - Continue supportive care as above and follow up as advised.

Quality checks:
- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - Allergies: not documented.
  - Comprehensive medications reconciliation (dosing and routes for vitamin D and ibuprofen not documented).
  - Vital signs and full physical examination findings not documented.
  - Family history not provided.
- Internal conflicts: None identified in the transcript.
- Transcript quality: Generally coherent; occasional repetition and missing transient data (e.g., exact vitals, dose details) but sufficient for current H&P purposes.
